2609.37934.title: GRFBrain: Graph-Structured Rectified Flows for EEG Dynamic Modeling
2609.37934.paper_summary: Forecasting time-varying functional connectivity from electroencephalography (EEG) requires modeling both history-dependent trends and structured variability across channels. Conditional flow matching provides a framework for distributional forecasting, yet it remains unclear whether graph-informed source distributions offer practical advantages over isotropic noise and strong deterministic predictors. We introduce a graph-structured residual flow framework that separates conditional mean prediction from stochastic residual transport. A history-only predictor estimates the future connectivity graph, while a graph Gaussian source encodes dependencies derived from past connectivity through a Laplacian-based covariance. A conditional velocity field transports source samples to future graph residuals, with transport time explicitly distinguished from physical EEG time. Our study identifies the conditions and controls needed to distinguish useful residual transport from improvements attributable to deterministic prediction, learned representations, and sampling effects.
2609.37934.paper_summary_zh: 預測來自腦電圖 (EEG) 的時間變化功能連接性需要對歷史依賴的趨勢和跨通道的結構變異性進行建模。條件流匹配提供了一個分佈預測的框架，但目前尚不清楚圖形信息源分佈是否相較於各向同性噪聲和強決定性預測器具有實際優勢。我們引入了一個圖結構的殘差流框架，將條件均值預測與隨機殘差傳輸分開。一個僅基於歷史的預測器估計未來的連接圖，而圖高斯源則通過基於拉普拉斯的協方差編碼來自過去連接的依賴關係。一個條件速度場將源樣本傳輸到未來的圖殘差，傳輸時間與物理EEG時間明確區分。我們的研究確定了區分有用的殘差傳輸與歸因於決定性預測、學習表示和取樣效應的改進所需的條件和控制。
